test: arbiter backend swap (qwen3.8-27b local -> glm-5.3-flash, Zhipu API)
question: does replacing the local arbiter model change the benchmark?
protocol: same harness, same gates, same temperature (0.0) and seed (20261015); only HUIYAN_LLM_PROVIDER changed from local to zhipu

arbiter_decided_detail: NHANES hyperglycemia x cataract_any (gold replicated) -> YES
KNHANES hyperglycemia x cataract_any (gold replicated) -> YES
CHARLS hyperglycemia x cataract_any (gold uninformative) -> YES
why.interpretation: the arbiter touches 3 of 474 cells; every other decision is taken by the deterministic rule layer, the negative-control gate or the evidence-B+ gate. The model is therefore not a lever on benchmark performance, and the G2-vs-G0 difference belongs to the evidence gate, not to the LLM.

implication: Switching to a stronger or commercial model cannot rescue the external gap (G2 0.312 < rule layer 0.360). To make the LLM matter, the gate would have to hand it more decisions (e.g. arbitrate all rule hits without B+ evidence), which is a protocol change and would need pre-registration; the standalone-LLM arm already showed that path degrades precision (0.10).
